title: Catalyst permission engine and runtime auth interceptor
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a new permissive, low-latency policy evaluation service (Catalyst) plus a compact runtime authorization interceptor that can be inserted into API, runtime, and console request paths. Catalyst will evaluate RBAC v2 policies, surface explainability metadata for audit logs, and support local cache/fast-path decisions for common allow/deny patterns. The interceptor will be language-agnostic, ship as a small Go binary and WASM module for console plugins, and provide consistent enforcement across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket covers the MVP: engine prototype, interceptor API, audit enrichment, and an initial canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Catalyst service exposes /evaluate REST endpoint with JSON request/response and <=3ms median eval for cached policies on p3-standard workload
Interceptor integrates with runtime request pipeline and can block/allow with <5ms median added latency in canary setup
Audit logs include policy_id, decision, matched_clauses, principal_id, resource, request_path, and an explainability token for reconcilers
Policy format supports role, action, resource patterns, time conditions, and delegation chains (v2 schema v0.9)
Automated unit + integration tests for policy parsing, caching TTL behavior, and failure-mode fallback to allowlist (configurable)
Security review completed and secrets handling documented (KMS/HSM integration for RBAC keys)
Canary rolled out to 5% of runtime traffic, telemetry dashboards showing decision latency and error rate established
design_notes: Engine: use a compact decision DAG compiled from high-level RBAC rules. Compiler emits a serialized decision graph that can be cached per-model-version. This reduces repeated AST traversal costs.

Caching strategy: two-layer cache. Hot key prefix cache keyed on principal+resource+action for 10s; policy artifact cache keyed on policy hash with TTL 1h. Cache invalidation hooks via policy-change webhook.

Fail-open vs fail-closed: default to fail-open for non-admin user paths to minimize customer impact, but configurable per-route and enforced by admin policy. Critical admin console operations default to fail-closed.

Telemetry/observability: tag decisions with eval_path and codegen_version so regressions can be traced back to policy compiler changes. Emit sampling of explainability tokens (P0 sampling for admin ops) to logs and secure storage.

Auth interceptor: implement as middleware with two delivery modes: local in-process library (Go) for runtime services and sidecar/remote call for language runtimes that cannot link native binary. WASM module will power browser/console plugins for UI-level gating.

SSO/SAML integration: map SAML assertions to principal identities and transient attributes. Ensure aliasing rules are deterministic and testable. OIDC mapping already available will be reused where possible.
Audit format: JSONL with structured fields; ensure logs are compat with existing audit ingestion pipeline (audit-sink v1). Add new fields under 'rbac_v2' namespace to avoid collisions.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Lab validation - unit/integration tests, run synthetic traffic harness against p3-standard cluster (complete)
Phase 1: Internal canary - route 1% non-critical production control-plane requests through interceptor for 48h. Monitor latency and decision parity vs legacy system.
Phase 2: Customer canary - enable interceptor for a small set (2) of low-risk customers with opt-in. Validate audit log schema and key rotation behavior.
Phase 3: Gradual ramp - increase to 20% with feature flags for fail-open vs fail-closed modes; run a 2-week observation window.
Phase 4: Global rollout - enable by default for Hosted API and Dedicated; provide upgrade guide for Private customers and migration tool for policy format conversion.
test_plan: Unit tests for policy compiler: 95% branch coverage on rule compilation paths
Integration tests for interceptor: simulate authn/auditing pipelines and assert decision parity with reference evaluator
Performance tests: p95 eval latency <12ms cold, <3ms warm with hot cache on representative traffic traces
Chaos tests: Catalyst returns 5xx; verify interceptor fallback behavior and end-to-end SLO preservation
End-to-end audit verification: ingest audit logs into staging audit-sink; assert schema compatibility and retention tags
